El Cañaveral — Madrid, Spain

Higher caution advised day Higher caution advised night

In detail

El Canaveral has extensive and very recent (2025-2026) documented coverage of serious organised crime: a robbery wave by the so-called 'banda de la alcantarilla' (July 2025) that led residents to demand a local police station, and multiple reports (November 2025 onward) of the Venezuelan organised-crime group 'Tren de Aragua' establishing a base in the neighbourhood involving occupied flats, drug production and prostitution, described by ABC as turning the development into 'la urbanizacion maldita' (the cursed development). Thirteen arrests were reported in one related operation. Sources checked: Antena3, 23 Jul 2025; LaSexta, 22 Jul 2025; ABC, 19 Nov 2025 ('urbanizacion maldita'); gaceta.es, 18 Nov 2025 (Tren de Aragua); Telemadrid, 8 Nov 2025; ABC, 15 Feb 2026.

Is El Cañaveral safe?

Wandroz currently rates El Cañaveral in Madrid as an area where the data suggests extra caution relative to other neighbourhoods in Madrid during the day and an area where the data suggests extra caution relative to other neighbourhoods in Madrid at night. This comes from a structured local-source assessment: an area-level review of credible local sources — local and national news, municipal and police-published material, and official surveys where they exist — consolidated across sources rather than taken from a single report. Is El Cañaveral safe at night?

At night, El Cañaveral is rated as an area where the data suggests extra caution relative to other neighbourhoods in Madrid. If you're unsure, it's worth checking recent local reviews for your specific street or block, since a neighbourhood-wide rating can't capture block-by-block variation.

El Cañaveral's day rating (an area where the data suggests extra caution relative to other neighbourhoods in Madrid) is the more relevant one for typical daytime tourist activity; check the night rating too if you'll be out late.
